Temp files were redirected to my scratch.

VAL CALL SITES: scripts/blocks_eval.py:147-148 already passes a per-item domain (it['domain']). But when it['path'] is None it writes the problem with B.write_problem (blocks_eval.py:142-144), which hardcodes '(:domain blocksworld-4ops)' (blocks.py:141); Logistics would need M.write_problem (mystery.py:166). B.parse_problem is regex-based and Blocksworld-oriented; M.parse_problem (mystery.py:151-163) is generic and parses all Logistics instances, including single-atom goals.

GENERIC EXECUTOR CAVEATS (bwmn/mystery.py): parse_domain, execute and bfs_plan are generic STRIPS and handle Logistics, with two problems. (1) ground() rejects any action with a repeated object (mystery.py:206), but VAL accepts e.g. (drive-truck t l l c). The published plans contain 51 such actions in 41 plans, and M.execute disagrees with the published VAL flag on 9 of them. A variant that allows repeats agreed with VAL on all 1,450 plans. (2) ground_actions/bfs_plan ground over untyped permutations of all objects: about 315k candidates for a 24-object instance, versus 14-720 type-consistent actions. A typed grounder is needed for any Logistics oracle or data generator.

scouts.topic: Published reference numbers for PlanBench Logistics plan generation (frontier LLMs/LRMs, verifier-in-loop, and domain-trained small models), to support roadmap item 9 (recipe transfer to Logistics)
findings: SUMMARY: Only two primary sources report plan generation on the actual PlanBench Logistics instances. (1) Valmeekam et al., NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv 2305.15771): GPT-4 gets 7.5-14%. (2) Strawberry Fields (arXiv 2410.02162): o1-preview gets 94% zero-shot in PDDL and 52% on the randomized-name version. I found no verified PlanBench-Logistics number for DeepSeek-R1, Claude, GPT-4o or LLaMA. No published fine-tuned small model has been tested on the PlanBench Logistics instance IDs. All trained-model Logistics results use the authors' own generated or IPC sets. Wherever those papers test larger instances than they trained on, they report failure: 0-14% out of distribution.

LOCAL EVIDENCE, almost no Logistics content. (a) research/_raw_research_2026-10-07.json has 10 'logistics' hits. They cover only PDDL-Instruct (Llama-3-8B 79% vs 11% baseline; GPT-4 78%) at [4]/claims[15], [5]/claims[9], [6]/verdicts[12] and [7]/verdicts[9], and SiGPlan at [0]/claims[30]. (b) research/SOLUTIONS_AND_BENCHMARK_PLAN.md never mentions Logistics. (c) bench/: grep -ril logistics finds 0 files, find -iname '*logistic*' finds 0 paths, and bench/planbench/LEDGER.json has 26 keys, none for Logistics. The vendored copy (SOURCE.md, commit fc638a1) contains only Blocksworld, Blocksworld-Hard, Mystery and unsolvable assets. (d) Item 9 is set in research/JOINT_ROADMAP_2026-10-08.md line 38 and DECISIONS.md line 765.

THE PLANBENCH LOGISTICS INSTANCE SET. I sparse-cloned upstream karthikv792/LLMs-Planning at the same commit fc638a1aff7d (2025-09-17) into scratch/llmsp. plan-bench/configs/logistics.yaml says n_instances: 285 (start 1, end 285). However, instances/logistics/generated_basic holds 286 files (instance-1..286). prompts/logistics/task_1_plan_generation.json holds 285 one-shot instances with ids 2..286, and the example for id i is instance i-1. Sizes from my scratch/scripts/lstats.py: 2-3 cities (43 x 2, 243 x 3), one truck and one airport per city, 1-3 locations per city (2-9 in total), 1-7 packages (100 instances have 7), 1-3 airplanes, 8-24 objects. Every package appears in the goal. The ground_truth_plan field has 3-48 steps (mean 24.1, median 25), and every plan has the same length as in the plan-optimality task file (0/285 mismatches), which suggests they are optimal. Plans are therefore much longer than in the B2 Blocksworld training range. The upstream README leaderboard has no Logistics column, and plan-bench/results/ contains only blocksworld, blocksworld_3, mystery_blocksworld and mystery_blocksworld_3, so no per-instance Logistics LLM outputs are published. The PlanBench D&B paper (arXiv 2206.10498v4) says 'We generate 285 instances for this domain' but reports only Blocksworld results. The v2 preprint (Oct 2022) also has no Logistics results; I checked by pdftotext.

Valmeekam et al., 'On the Planning Abilities of LLMs: A Critical Investigation', NeurIPS 2023, arXiv 2305.15771v2. I checked the PDF text in scratch/dl_2305/p.txt. p.7: 'We generated 200 instances on this domain' (200, not 285; which 200 is not stated). Zero-/one-shot, single plan, checked with VAL. NL prompts (Table 1, p.5): GPT-4 one-shot 28/200 (14%), zero-shot 15/200 (7.5%). GPT-3.5 1/200 (0.5%) both. Instruct-GPT3.5 one-shot 6/200 (3%). Instruct-GPT3 (text-davinci-002) one-shot 3/200 (1.5%). PDDL prompts (Table 2, p.6): GPT-4 one-shot 28/200 (14%), zero-shot 11/200 (5.5%). GPT-3.5 one-shot 1/200, zero-shot 0/200. The p.7 prose restates the GPT-4 numbers. No CoT or fine-tuning on Logistics; GPT-3 was fine-tuned only on Blocksworld.

Same paper, verifier-in-loop regime. Table 4 (p.9): GPT-4 back-prompted by VAL solves 35/50 (70%) of Logistics instances it had already failed one-shot in NL, within a 15-round cap, averaging 3.31 feedback rounds. Table 3 (p.8) plus footnote 4: using GPT-4 plans as LPG seeds averages 51.3 search steps, against 77.5 for an empty seed and 144.39 for a random seed, on the 179 instances solvable in under 550 steps. In LLMs Still Can't Plan; Can LRMs? (arXiv 2409.13373v1), Logistics appears only as a citation of this 70%.

Valmeekam, Stechly, Gundawar, Kambhampati, 'Planning in Strawberry Fields', arXiv 2410.02162v1 (only version). I checked the PDF text in scratch/dl_2410/s.txt. Table 2 (p.5), zero-shot over 200 Logistics instances: o1-preview 94%, average 84.07 s per instance; o1-mini not run ('-'); Fast Downward 100%, 0.13 s. On 200 'Randomized Mystery Logistics' instances: o1-preview 52%, 167.41 s; FD 100%. Counts of 188/200 and 104/200 are my derivation. p.5 text: 'o1-preview solves 94% of all 200 problems tested and achieves 52% on the obfuscated variant'. Appendix K (pp.24-26) shows the prompt is zero-shot PDDL, and its example problem is logistics-c2-s1-p1-a2, which is PlanBench instance-1. Which 200 of the 285 were used is not stated. This is the frontier LRM reference for the same instance distribution.

NOT VERIFIED: DeepSeek-R1 (and any other LRM) on PlanBench Logistics. The TMLR 2025 version ('A Systematic Evaluation of the Planning and Scheduling Abilities of the Reasoning Model o1', openreview FkKBxp0FhR; mlanthology lists the PDF as openreview.net/pdf/1eaa842b...) says in its abstract that it evaluates DeepSeek R1. Both WebFetch and curl got the OpenReview bot check (HTTP 403), so I could not confirm whether it reports R1 on Logistics. The upstream README leaderboard lists R1 only on the Blocksworld variants.

Huang and Zhang, 'On the Limit of Language Models as Planning Formalizers', ACL 2025 main (arXiv 2412.09879v4). Logistics-100 uses IPC 1998/2000 instances, which are not PlanBench and are larger. It is zero-shot and checked with VAL. Table 4 (Appendix D.3) gives LLM-as-planner correctness for Natural / Moderately / Heavily templated descriptions: DeepSeek-R1 12/22/22 of 100; o3-mini 14/21/21; gpt-4o 1/0/0; gpt-4o-mini 0/0/0; gpt-3.5-turbo 0/0/0; Llama-3.1-8B 1/0/0; Llama-3.1-70B 0/0/0; gemma-2-9b 0/0/0; gemma-2-27b 0/0/1. In the LLM-as-formalizer setting (LLM writes PDDL, a planner solves it), correctness is R1 9/73/64, o3-mini 7/39/47 and gpt-4o 2/13/13. This is the only verified DeepSeek-R1 Logistics number I found.

AoT+ (Sel et al., 'LLMs Can Plan Only If We Tell Them', ICLR 2025, arXiv 2501.13545v1), Table 3, Logistics accuracy in %. The setup 'closely follow[s] those in Valmeekam et al. (2023)'; the instance count is not stated. CoT: GPT-4 14, GPT-4o 16, Claude 27, Gemini 1.5 8B/Flash/Pro 6/7/16, LLaMA-3.1 8B/70B/405B 2/7/5. LLM-Modulo (verifier loop): GPT-4 70, GPT-4o 56, Claude 26, Gemini 3/5/8, LLaMA 4/16/30. AoT: 24/34/41, Gemini 8/11/24, LLaMA 5/13/32. AoT+ (prompting only, no verifier): GPT-4 80, GPT-4o 70, Claude 53, Gemini 19/24/57, LLaMA-3.1 14/71/75. Caveat: the GPT-4 LLM-Modulo value of 70 equals the 35/50 failed-subset number in 2305.15771, so it may be copied rather than re-measured. 'Claude' is not given a version.

AutoPlanBench (Stein, Fiser, Hoffmann, Koller; arXiv 2311.09830v4, May 2025; venue not shown). It uses GPT-4o on 20 PlanBench Logistics problems (Appendix B: 'domain PDDL files and problems from the PlanBench repository'). Table 2, solved out of 20. Open-loop few-shot: Basic 5, CoT 10. Closed-loop with a simulator returning observations after every action: Act 16, ReAct 19. PDDL-input Basic 6, Act 15. The row for Valmeekam's hand-written NL encodings reads 3/5/17/12; I inferred that column mapping from the text. BrFS, LM-cut and FF each solve 20/20. Act and ReAct use environment feedback, so they are a different regime.

Armony, Merono-Penuela, Canal, 'How Far Are LLMs from Symbolic Planners?', arXiv 2508.01300v1. Low confidence: n is not stated, and instances only plausibly come from PlanBench ('PlanBench-generated JSONs'). VAL-valid rate of the raw LLM plan on Logistics, Table A.6, given as one-shot / PDDL / state-tracking / zero-shot: o4-mini 0.89/0.90/0.34/0.45; o3-mini 0.30/0.91/0.19/0.42; Claude 3.7 Sonnet 0.28/0.21/0.01/0.31; Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.12/0.21/0.00/0.04; GPT-3.5-turbo 0.04/0.13/0.01/0.03. Random Logistics, o4-mini (Table A.4): one-shot 0.16, PDDL 0.89, zero-shot 0.12. The table values disagree slightly with each other (o4-mini PDDL is 0.91 in A.4 and 0.90 in A.6).

Bohnet et al., 'Exploring and Benchmarking the Planning Capabilities of LLMs', arXiv 2406.13094v2 (Nov 2024; venue not listed). Own generated Logistics, solved by Fast Downward and checked with a VAL-style verifier. Few-shot (Sec 3.1.1): 'The 1-shot planning capability of Gemini 1.5 Pro reaches 43% for PDDL and for Natural Language 48%'; GPT-4 Turbo values appear only in Fig. 2. Fine-tuned Gemini 1.0 S (Table 1, Table 4, App. C; 13,483 training and 500 test samples per split, Table 12): trained on 1-2 packages it scores 99.8% in distribution but 10.8% (54/500) on 3-5 packages. Trained on 3-5 packages it scores 63.4% (317/500) in distribution and 98.0% on 1-2. The in-context rows of Table 4 (e.g. Gemini 1.5 Pro 30-shot: 56.4 / 11.3 and 62.7 / 8.04) are hard to interpret; I did not verify their column mapping.

Test: 1,000 in-distribution problems; the paper notes 'PlanBench has at most 24 objects', which matches my count. Table 2: completion 99.30% at N=10 and 99.70% at N=10^3, mean plan length 146 vs 165 for FD-LAMA-first. Table 3: 95/169 optimal on the commonly solved subset. Extrapolation coverage is 0.00 for every model including PlanGPT (Table 2, 7-15 goals); the best interpolation score is .44+/-.09, and that column mapping is uncertain. scouts.topic: Item 9 (PlanBench Logistics): which parts of the BWM code can be reused, and whether Logistics prompts fit the 256/640-token max-len and the 40-token delta cap
findings: VERDICT. The search machinery and the LM utilities work for any domain. Everything that touches the state, prompt or action format is Blocksworld-only. Logistics needs one new pure-python domain module, one new planner-wrapper module that leaves the pinned file alone, and six new scripts (copies with Logistics constants). lm.py and train_generic.py are reused unchanged. Token fit: 256 fits no Logistics row at any size. 640 fits every F row. It fits proposer rows only if targets are truncated, or if training stays at 3 or fewer packages. The 40-token delta cap fits (at most 25 tokens).

ASSETS. Logistics is NOT vendored in the project. bench/planbench holds only blocksworld, blocksworld_hard, instances_mystery and unsolvable_blocksworld (SOURCE.md line 6). The only local copy is an LLMs-Planning clone in another session's scratchpad: C:/Users/clclc/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-clclc-BusinessProject-WorldModel-Rineya-BWM-001-Research-Bundle/bc6adc92-8f02-442d-b75d-8a2ed62c0851/scratchpad/LLMs-Planning/plan-bench/instances/logistics. It is at the same upstream commit as SOURCE.md (fc638a1aff7d…, from git log). The Task 1 test set is generated_basic instances 2..286 (285 instances; instance 1 is the one-shot example): prompts/logistics/task_1_plan_generation.json, and configs/logistics.yaml n_instances 285. All 285 ground-truth plans succeed under an exact executor. VAL (bench/planbench/VAL/bin/validate/validate.exe) prints 'Plan valid' for the instance-2 ground-truth plan with the Logistics domain, so B.val_check(problem, plan, domain_path=...) is reusable. The Task 5 ground-truth plans in that clone do NOT match the local generated/ PDDL: 0/12 execute, and they use locations like l2-8 that don't exist locally.

INSTANCE SIZES (Task 1, 285 instances; my script lg_size.py). Objects 8-24 (median 21). Cities 2-3, 1-3 locations per city, trucks 2-3, airplanes 1-3. Packages 1-7: by count 1:23, 2:24, 3:26, 4:23, 5:42, 6:47, 7:100 instances. Facts per state: 12-36 static (type predicates, in-city, airport) plus 4-12 dynamic (at/in, exactly one per mobile object), so the state size is constant along a plan. Goals are 1-7 'at' facts, one per package. Ground-truth plan length 3-48 (median 25, p90 37; 19-48 at 7 packages). Naming conventions hold in all 286 files: the airport is always lX-0, location lX-Y is in city cX, truck tX is in cX, planes start at airports. So object names reveal the map.

TOKEN METHOD. I counted exactly with the standalone `tokenizers` 0.22.2 library on the core's tokenizer.json. I checked sys.modules: no torch, transformers or peft gets imported. I validated it by replaying train_generic's row order: it reproduces the recorded tokens_processed and supervised_tokens exactly for BW_F_s0 (1,673,502 / 383,877), BW_Fdelta_s0 (1,551,649 / 175,624) and BW_Pa_v2_s1 (2,781,649 / 476,002) (runs/*/metrics.json). The chars/3.5 rule UNDER-estimates Logistics by about 25%: typed F prompt median 310 by chars/3.5 vs 390 exact. The reason is that Qwen splits digits ('l0-0' = 4 tokens, '"l0-0"' = 6, 'p12' = 3). A Logistics action costs about 13 tokens in the plan target (12.2-13.9) vs 5.3 for Blocksworld. Reference points: Blocksworld training rows maxed at 175 (F delta) and 246 (proposer), under max_len 256. Blocksworld-hard F prompts are 149-185 tokens.

TOKEN RESULTS (draft Logistics system prompts: forward 156 tokens, proposer 125, vs Blocksworld 85/71). F delta rows (prompt + target + EOS) at Task 1 sizes: 293-402 (map as lists, types implied by names), 313-446 (explicit type lists), 283-385 (compact obj->place dict). Already 293-362 at 1 package; mean 344 / max 386 at 1-4 packages. 256 fails for all 285; 640 fits all. Proposer prompts: 236-391 (named) / 256-435 (typed). Full-plan proposer rows: 286-1011 named / 309-1055 typed; 175/285 (named) and 193/285 (typed) instances exceed 640. At 1-4 packages: mean 428, max 749, 37 of 1,215 suffix rows over 640. Truncated targets fit 640: first 8/12/16 actions give max 509/563/615 tokens. lm.train_sft raises on ANY overlength row (lm.py lines 413-414), so the prereg must fix max_len plus truncation or explicit drop-and-count (the B3 precedent, DECISIONS.md lines 522-523). The mystery-style rules-in-prompt rendering (M.forward_prompt) costs 467-744 tokens, 203/285 over 640, so it is not usable as-is.

DELTA CAP AND GENERATION CAPS. The Logistics delta target is always one add and one del fact, e.g. {"add":["in p0 a1"],"del":["at p0 l1-0"],"legal":true}. It is at most 25 tokens (+EOS) on every Task 1 instance and every plan step, so the 40-token cap (blocks_planner.py line 73) fits; the docstring claim '<= 25 tokens' (lines 43-44) also holds for Logistics. The proposer caps do NOT carry over. The frozen B2 beam uses M=80 with R=12 and P=1 (runs/FREEZE_B2_beam.json); at 13 tokens per action, M=80 holds only about 5-6 actions, so R=12 needs M of about 160. The S-direct cap M=256 (bw_freeze.py line 47) would truncate 193/285 full ground-truth plans (targets 41-619 tokens); the D-48 'room for a complete plan' analogue is M of about 640-700. LMProposerBW's 120-token default (blocks_planner.py line 112) covers about 9 actions. blocks.parse_plan's 60-action cap (blocks.py line 406) is fine (Task 1 max is 48).

Its cache JSONL format is generic (lines 54-61, 83-87). It imports lm (line 20), and lm imports torch at module level (lm.py line 20), so even CPU harness runs of a wrapper import torch, as Blocksworld runs already do.

lm.py has nothing Blocksworld-specific and needs no change: encode_pair (313-321), collate, chunked_ce, train_sft (390-521), sample_crn_shared (571-653, used by LMProposerBW), sample_crn (657-736), greedy_shared_prefix (740-816). Caveats: (a) greedy_shared_prefix shares only the token prefix common to ALL prompts in a call (line 757). Canonical JSON key order (action < map < state) and rollout_many's cross-instance batching mean only the system prompt is shared (about 160 tokens); the map (33-76 tokens) and state (40-104) stay in each row's own suffix. Grouping per instance, with the map key sorted first, would be an optional optimisation inside a new F class. (b) The batch size there (line 770) and in sample_crn_shared (line 589) shrinks about 2x for Logistics prompt lengths. (c) Recorded Blocksworld peak memory was 2.64-2.90 GiB at max_len 256. bwmn/mystery.py (pure python) already has a generic STRIPS engine that is partly reusable. parse_domain parses the Logistics domain (6 actions plus type predicates). step/execute reproduce all 285 ground-truth plans. parse_action/parse_plan (lines 1062-1095) and write_problem(dom, …) (166-169) are generic given a Domain. (1) ground() rejects repeated objects (line 206), but VAL accepts self-loop moves: I ran VAL on 'fly-airplane a0 l1-0 l1-0' and 'drive-truck t1 l1-0 l1-0 c1' before the instance-2 plan, and both gave 'Plan valid', while mystery.applicable returned False. A Logistics executor and the F labels must follow VAL here, or the planner must ban these moves explicitly. (2) ground_actions is untyped: 265,650 ground actions for a 23-object instance vs 564 when typed, so bfs_plan is unusable for Logistics.

TEACHER FEASIBILITY (lg_bfs.py, typed BFS, 200k-state cap like blocks.bfs_plan). It solved every sampled instance with 1-4 packages (up to 60,767 states), and BFS length always equalled ground-truth length (the ground-truth plans are optimal). designs.name: LG-LEAN: train the Blocksworld recipe on 1-3-package generated Logistics problems, then test it once on 40 PlanBench Logistics instances with 4-7 packages, paired against S-direct
designs.question_and_claim:
QUESTION: Does the B2 recipe carry over to PlanBench Logistics unchanged in structure? The recipe is a goal-blind learned world model F (delta format), plus an outcome-conditioned proposer Pa, plus the pinned plan_beam searching in imagination, all trained only on small generated problems. Logistics is the item-9 choice (DECISIONS.md D-65 item 5, lines 765-766; JOINT_ROADMAP_2026-10-08.md line 38: "Learned F + search beats S-direct out of size range in a new domain").

PRIMARY CLAIM (H1): on 40 pre-registered PlanBench Logistics Task-1 instances with 4-7 packages, S-beam (F + Pa + plan_beam) solves more instances than S-direct (the same Pa, greedy, one plan, no F). Both models are trained only on generated problems with 1-3 packages. Test: paired exact McNemar, two-sided, alpha 0.05. Each system is run once and VAL-checked.

Why 1-3 packages: the test instances are out of range on goal count (4-7 vs at most 3), on package count, and on plan length. Optimal lengths in the test list are 13-41, mean 27.2 (scratch designer_lean/test40.py output). Generated 3-package A* plans are 3-26 steps (designer_lean/gaps_gen.py). The maps stay inside PlanBench's range (2-3 cities, 1-3 locations per city, 1-3 airplanes), so the out-of-range axis is packages, goals and plan length only. The ratio of 3 to 7 packages (2.3x) mirrors the Blocksworld ratio of 6 to 15 blocks (PREREG_PLANBENCH.md lines 86-88).

PRE-REGISTERED READING:
- "transfer: yes" requires b > c and p < 0.05.
- "strong" additionally requires S-beam >= 20/40.
- Anything else is "not supported".
- With n = 40, significance needs at least b = 6 at c = 0 (bwmn/stats.mcnemar_exact(6,0) = 0.031; (5,0) = 0.0625), so "yes" implies at least +15 pp.

What "same recipe" means, stated up front: the planner code is unchanged (bwmn/blocks_planner.py sha 18a5f22b…, pinned by D-63 line 664). So are the trainer (scripts/train_generic.py), lm.py, the LoRA recipe (batch 16, lr 1e-4) and the selection and freeze procedure. Only the domain module is new: the simulator used for labels, the renderer and the parser. That matches the Blocksworld split.

SYSTEMS (frozen, one plan per instance, no execution feedback):
- S-beam (primary): Titan-Sparse + LG_Fdelta_s0 + LG_Pa_s1, BP.plan_beam via lg_planner.
- S-direct (internal no-F arm): the same Pa, candidate 0 (greedy), BP.plan_direct. M = 704 gives room for a complete 48-action plan at about 14 tokens per action. This is the D-48 'room for a complete plan' analogue (DECISIONS.md lines 403-405; BW used M = 256, bw_freeze.py lines 46-47).

SELECTION GRID (scripts/lg_select.py, a copy of bw_select.py with a CountingF view over one shared memoised F, lines 28-36). Every pair is resumable per (config, set). K = 4 rather than B2's K = 8 is a LEAN choice: in BW_SELECT_v1/select.jsonl, K4 gave val_large 0.600 at 134.3 s per instance against 0.633 at 256.7 s for K8, and 0.98 on val_v2 for both. That is 95% of the success for 52% of the GPU.
- G1 'B2 transplant': K 4, W 4, E 24, R 12, M 184, P 1. M is 12 actions × 14 tokens + 16 overhead (B2 used M 80 for R 12, FREEZE_B2_beam.json).
- G2 'long window': K 4, W 4, E 24, R 24, M 352, P 1.

Why G2: the default unmet only drops when a package arrives. In generated A*-optimal plans, the largest gap between successive deliveries exceeded 12 steps in 9/40 three-package, 2/19 four-package and 1/6 five-package instances, and never exceeded 24 (max 21). Source: designer_lean/gaps_gen.py, generated instances only. Under R = 12 such a plateau advances the beam by only one step per round (blocks_planner.py line 320).

Max proposer tokens per instance (E×K×M): G1 17,664; G2 33,792.

S-direct is also measured on both sets but is not a selection candidate.

FROZEN RULE (scripts/lg_freeze.py, a copy of bw_freeze.py lines 30-36):
- Among G1 and G2 evaluated on val_in (30) and val_oor (20, pooling halves a and b), pick the higher mean success (val_in + val_oor)/2.
- Constraint: at most 2,000 unique F queries per instance on each set. If neither config meets it, take the one with fewer F queries on val_oor.
- If the means differ by 0.025 or less, take the one with fewer proposer tokens per instance.
- The freeze writes FREEZE_LG_beam.json and FREEZE_LG_direct.json with the adapter SHA-256s, the PREREG_LOGISTICS.md SHA, the test-list SHA and the SHAs of blocks_planner.py, blocks.py, lm.py, logistics.py and lg_planner.py.

- On NO-GO the test is not run, all 285 instances stay reserved, and "transfer not supported on generated out-of-range problems" is reported.
- Any revised recipe requires a new addendum and is selected on generated sets again.

ESTIMATES, scaled from measured BW runs; Logistics tokens per action run 13.0-13.8 against 5.3, and prompts are about 2x longer:
- TRAINING:
  - F: 2.5M tokens at 250-300 tok/s ≈ 2.3-2.8 h.
  - Pa: 3.2M tokens at 190-286 tok/s ≈ 3.1-4.7 h.
  - Total 5.4-7.5 h. Rates: BW_Pa_v2_s1 187.9, BW_Pa_v3_s1 249.6 at max-len 640, BW_Fdelta_s0 261.2 tok/s.
- SELECTION:
  - S-direct on both sets plus G1/G2 on val_in ≈ 0.4 h (BW val_v2 beam K8 took 5.1 s per instance).
  - val_oor G1: 20 × 300-550 s ≈ 1.7-3.1 h. Basis: BW val_large K4 R12 M80 took 134.3 s per instance at 3,618 proposer tokens and 143.7 F queries; Logistics is estimated at 2.3-4x.

- TEST: S-direct about 0.1 h; S-beam 40 × 300-800 s ≈ 3.3-8.9 h, in 4 shards of 10, each at most about 2.2 h.

TURN MAP:
- L1: smoke + F + Pa start.
- L2: Pa finish + direct/val_in + G1 val_oor_a.
- L3: rest of the selection.
- L4: S-direct + S-beam shards 0-1, or 0-3 if fast.
- L5: remaining shards.
The selection measures the selected config's cost per instance before the test; this changes only the shard plan, never the settings.

ZERO-GPU WORK (CPU lane, one lane, 6 threads): data generation, the harness, the F audit (12 GB RAM floor), freeze, analysis.

SAVINGS vs a straight B2 copy: K 4 instead of 8 (about -48% beam cost, measured on BW); Pa 600 steps instead of 1,000 (about -2-3 h); n = 40 instead of 212 (about -80% test cost); a 2-config grid; no mirror run; no exact-F test arm; and the gate that avoids burning about 2 test turns on a broken system.
risks: F extrapolation: F is trained on 1-3-package states (F rows at most 316 tokens) but must simulate 4-7-package states (up to 399 tokens). A small per-step error rate compounds over 13-41-step plans. Mitigation: the CPU F audit by package count before selection. BW precedent: delta F trained on 3-6 blocks scored 1.000 exact at 10 blocks (runs/BW_Fdelta_s0/grade_size.json). A shortfall here is a reported result, not a re-tune.

Search plateau: the default unmet = |goal - state| drops only when a package arrives. Generated optimal plans have delivery gaps over 12 steps in about 10-22% of instances (gaps_gen.py), and under R = 12 the beam then advances one step per round (blocks_planner.py line 320). G2 (R 24) is in the grid. No Logistics heuristic is added, because the claim requires the domain-agnostic planner.

Compute overrun: the 300-800 s per-instance estimate is an extrapolation with a factor-2 uncertainty. Mitigation: the per-instance cost is measured during selection, the test is split into 4 shards, val_oor is split in halves, and checkpoint resume covers training. Shared-GPU incidents (2 reboots on 2026-10-10, I-16/I-17) can cut turns; shards restart with warm caches.

Proposer goal-count extrapolation: Pa is trained on at most 3 goals and must handle 4-7, so it may ignore some goals. The beam builds partial progress across expansions, and BW worked with goals of 1-5 pairs vs 5-12 (D-43). S-direct is expected to be weak; this is the comparison the claim needs, not a confound.

Low power: with n = 40, only large effects are detectable (b of at least 6 at c = 0), and the per-stratum n of 10 gives wide CIs. Claims are restricted to the pooled primary test. The remaining 172 out-of-range and 73 in-range instances stay reserved for a confirmation prereg.

designs.question_and_claim:
QUESTION. Does the B2 recipe transfer to a second PlanBench domain? The recipe: a goal-blind delta world model F plus an outcome-conditioned proposer Pa, as two unmerged LoRAs on frozen Titan-Sparse 0.6B FP32, with beam search in imagination, no execution feedback, one plan per instance, and planner settings selected only on generated sets. Transfer means world model plus search beats the same proposer alone OUTSIDE the training size range.

DESIGN AXIS. Package count is the only out-of-range dimension. Training covers PlanBench's full ranges of cities (2-3), city size (1-3) and airplanes (1-3, never more than cities), but only 1-3 packages. Test is 4-7 packages, up to 2.33x the training maximum. FD-optimal plan length is 3-24 in range versus 12-48 out of range (designer/strata.py).

REGISTERED PRIMARY (P1). On PB-OUT (PlanBench Logistics t1 IDs 2-286 with 4-7 packages, n=212), S-beam minus S-direct must be at least +0.20, with exact two-sided McNemar p < 0.01.

READINGS
- YES: P1 holds AND the standardized PB-OUT minus MIRROR S-beam gap is at most +10 pp.
- PARTIAL: P1 holds but the mirror flag is raised, OR P1 fails while secondary S1 (the same contrast on the generated mirror) holds.
- NO: otherwise. A NO is reported as 'the recipe did not transfer at this budget', together with the out-of-range F accuracy.

ALLOWED CLAIMS (YES only)
- 'Trained only on generated Logistics problems with <=3 packages, a frozen 0.6B Rineya with two LoRA adapters, planning without feedback, solves X/212 PlanBench Logistics instances with 4-7 packages (CI). The same proposer without the world model solves Y/212 (paired McNemar p).'
- 'The training hyperparameters were those of B2 (steps, batch, lr, LoRA), with only max_len changed. The planner was re-selected on generated sets. The recipe transferred across two PlanBench domains.'
- Published numbers on identical IDs may be quoted only with the regime caveat (zero- or one-shot generalists).

NOT ALLOWED
- 'domain-general planner' or 'general world model'. There are two domains, with per-domain adapters, generators and parsers.
- 'beats o1-preview' (117/127 on PB-OUT-A).
- 'beats GPT-4 at planning' without the regime caveat.
- Any comparison to verifier-in-loop numbers: GPT-4+VAL 35/50, LLM-Modulo, AoT+ Modulo.
- Any statement about obfuscated or Mystery Logistics.
- 'zero-shot'.
- Calling PB-IN results out-of-range.
- Seed-robust wording before Stage 2.
- Any claim from a configuration selected on PB instances.
- FLOP-matched claims against API models.
- 'Logistics solved' (Fast Downward solves 100%).

WHY IT IS NOT TRIVIAL. Published SFT size extrapolation on Logistics collapses:
- Bohnet et al. 2406.13094: 99.8% falls to 10.8% when trained on 1-2 packages and tested on 3-5.
- Huang/Lipovetzky/Cohn 2412.10675: 100% falls to 14.0% on 17-32-action plans.
- Fritzsche et al. 2508.07743: 0.00 extrapolation coverage.
- On PB-OUT itself, the best GPT-4 setting gets 8/128.
designs.domain_representation:
INTERNAL STATE
- The full PDDL fact frozenset: static facts (types, in-city, airport) plus dynamic facts (at, in).
- Parsed with B.parse_problem, which is generic and identical to M.parse_problem on all 286 files (scout).
- States are therefore self-contained hashable keys for plan_beam's seen-set and the F memo/cache.
- Internally, actions are PDDL op tuples.

SEMANTICS (new pure-python bwmn/logistics.py) follow VAL:
- Delete-then-add.
- Self-loop drive/fly is a legal no-op. VAL says 'Plan valid' for scout files plan_selfloop*.txt.
- mystery.ground is NOT reused: it rejects repeated objects (mystery.py line 206) and disagrees with VAL on 9 published plans.
- An illegal action leaves the state unchanged and is labelled legal=false (BWM convention).
- A typed grounder is used: 14-720 actions per instance, versus about 265k-315k untyped.

LM RENDERING. Compact canonical JSON via B.canonical with sorted keys. Types come from the group, so names need not reveal them:
{"map":{"airports":["l0-0","l1-0"],"cities":{"c0":["l0-0","l0-1"],"c1":[...]}},"packages":{"p0":"l0-1","p3":"t0"},"planes":{"a0":"l1-0"},"trucks":{"t0":"l0-1"}}
- F prompt adds "action".
- Pa prompt adds "goal":{"p0":"l1-2",...} and "outcome":"success" (B2 outcome conditioning).
- System prompts state the rules, as B2 does: F 110 tokens, Pa 80 tokens (Blocksworld: 85 and 71).

ACTION SURFACE. Merged verbs, following the PlanBench NL convention 'load {} into {} at {}' (configs/logistics.yaml lines 62-70):
- "load p0 t0 l0-1", "unload p0 a1 l1-0", "drive t0 l0-1 l0-0 c0", "fly a0 l0-0 l1-0".
- The parser maps verb + vehicle type (from the problem's type facts) to the PDDL op, and checks arity and object types. Anything else returns None.
- Cost: 11.0 tokens per action, versus 13.0 with PDDL op names (designer/rep_cost.py, on PB GT plans).
- Parse cap: 96 actions (Blocksworld's is 60).

F OUTPUT. The B2 delta format, reusing B.forward_target_delta and B.parse_forward_delta unchanged, e.g. {"add":["in p0 a1"],"del":["at p0 l1-0"],"legal":true}. It is at most 25 tokens (scout), so it fits the 40-token F cap in blocks_planner.

MEASURED EXACT TOKEN COUNTS (tokenizers library on the core tokenizer.json; no torch):
- Generated rows with <=3 packages (designer/gen_rows.py): F rows mean 284, max 329. Pa full-suffix rows mean 315, p99 503, max 567; 0 of 3,329 exceed 640.
- Test time on PB-OUT: F prompt + delta at most 353 tokens. Pa prompt at most 341.
- Full-suffix rows would reach 865 at 4-7 packages. So the no-F arm must generate beyond its training length, which is intended.
- max_len is 640 for both adapters; this is the only change from B2's 256. Overlength rows are dropped and counted before training, because lm.train_sft raises on them (lm.py lines 413-414). Expected count: 0.

NAMING
- PlanBench names leak the map: lX-0 is the airport, lX-Y is in cX, tX is in cX.
- 50% of training instances keep the PlanBench convention. 50% are renamed with random location and vehicle indices, and airports are not index 0, so the explicit map must be read.
- Package names are always drawn from the pool p0..p11, so the test names p3..p6 occur in training. This follows the a..o precedent (blocks_data.py line 8).

GENERATOR (new; reproduces the distribution in logistics.c lines 217-243)
- Truck i sits in city i at a random location.
- Package origins and goals are uniform over all locations.
- Planes start at a random city's airport.
- Every package has a goal, as in PlanBench (goal size = package count on 286/286).
- Shapes are uniform over cities {2,3} x city size {1,2,3} x planes {1..cities}; packages uniform over {1,2,3}.
- Instances whose goal already holds in the initial state are skipped.
- Seeds: 20261101 train, 20261102 VAL, 20261103 MIRROR, 20261104 PERM. This avoids RCX's 202612xx range.

TEACHER: A* with an admissible h0 (load/unload lower bound + per-package move bound).
- It is optimal: on all 26 three-package PlanBench instances its length equals the FD astar(lmcut) GT, max 1.3 s (designer/teacher_timing.out).
- On 600 generated instances with <=3 packages: 0 failures, median 0.002 s, max 29.5 s, optimal length up to 27 (designer/gen_proto.py).
- BFS is not used: it fails 2 of 26 three-package PlanBench instances at a 400k-state cap.
- A 30 s timeout applies, with drop-and-count.

EXCLUSION. A renaming-invariant canonical signature (designer/canon.py) brute-forces city permutations x within-city non-airport location permutations (at most 48 maps) and treats vehicles and packages as multisets.
- It gives 285 classes over the 286 PlanBench files (the only duplicate pair is 47/48), and the renaming-invariance check passed.
- Any instance whose signature matches a PlanBench signature (all 286) is dropped: 36/600 = 6% at <=3 packages.
- Within-sample duplicates are dropped: 68/600 = 11%.
- Suffix rows whose (state, goal) signature hits PlanBench are dropped, using the B2 guard (blocks_data.py lines 80-84).
- Train and validation are split by signature (8% val, B2 lines 59-66).
- Package count is a signature invariant, so 4-7-package test sets cannot collide with training.

F ROWS. 12,000 delta rows, the B2 count.
- Start at a uniformly chosen state on the teacher plan. B2's comment at blocks_data.py line 107 states this intent, but its code starts at init; this deviation is declared.
- Take 0-7 random legal steps.
- Then pick a legal action (50%) or an illegal one (50%), uniformly from the typed ground actions, which include self-loops.
- Labels come from the VAL-semantics executor.

PA ROWS. 6,000 train instances (B2 v2 recipe):
- every suffix of the optimal plan, with outcome=success;
- one noisy plan per instance: one action replaced by a random typed ground action, outcome labelled by exact execution.
